fields.quote: Retry filtering makes every delivery exactly once
fields.rationale: source.contracts[1] says a send rejection may happen after the remote side effect commits and that there is no deduplication or idempotency contract. source.contracts[3] says separate calls share no retry counter or cross-call exclusion. probe-results.json results.after.duplicate.effects is 2 after a retryable rejection that already recorded an effect. results.after.concurrentCalls sums to 2 effects. The title states a universal exactly-once guarantee. Adjacent qualifications in /dek, /footer, and /sections/2 do not cancel a false title. source.body records exactly-once as what the author says, not as a verified property. Passing modeled successes do not prove that guarantee.
source.json title is "Cedar Relay: filter retries and increase delays". The eyebrow repeats that product name.

fields.quote: Permanent failures stop immediately; retryable failures use increasing requested delays without a delivery deduplication guarantee.
fields.rationale: after() throws when !error.retryable. probe-results.json results.after.permanent has calls 1, delays [], error "permanent". results.after.exhausted.delays is [10, 20], matching sleep(10 * 2 ** attempt) on attempts 0 and 1. source.contracts[1] denies a deduplication guarantee. source.contracts[2] says delays are requested milliseconds, which matches "requested delays".
probe-results.json assumptions state: "Deterministic modeled send outcomes and immediate sleep promises; no timing or production measurement." The meta names that evidence class.

fields.quote: A rejected acknowledgment can still follow a committed remote effect.
fields.rationale: source.contracts[1]: "A send rejection may happen after the remote side effect commits." probe.mjs duplicate scenario passes { effect: true, error: transient } on the first send. results.after.duplicate and results.before.duplicate each record effects 2.
Section label only. It does not assert a property of the functions, contracts, or probes.

fields.quote: The old loop retried every rejection
fields.rationale: before() retries any caught send error until attempt === retries. It does not read error.retryable. probe-results.json results.before.permanent.calls is 2 after a non-retryable error. results.before.exhausted.calls is 3 after retryable errors.

fields.quote: The old loop retried rejected sends until the retry budget ran out. It requested a ten-millisecond delay between attempts.
fields.rationale: before() sleeps only when attempt !== retries, then continues the loop. sleep(10) is the only delay. results.before.exhausted has calls 3 and delays [10, 10]. results.before.zeroBudget has calls 1 and delays [], so the last rejection is not followed by a sleep. source.contracts[2] treats those values as requested milliseconds.
Section label only. It does not assert a property of the functions, contracts, or probes.

after() inspects error.retryable in the catch path before await sleep(10 * 2 ** attempt). A non-retryable error throws without sleep. results.after.permanent.delays is []. results.after.exhausted.delays is [10, 20] only after retryable errors.

fields.quote: The changed loop stops on a non-retryable error. With a budget of two retries, retryable failures request delays of 10 then 20 milliseconds before the final send. This permits up to three sends. A rejected sleep prevents the next send.
fields.rationale: The non-retryable clause is results.after.permanent: calls 1, error "permanent", delays []. For retries=2, attempt runs 0..2 so three sends are possible; results.after.exhausted.calls is 3 and delays are [10, 20], which is 10 * 2 ** 0 then 10 * 2 ** 1 before the final send. source.contracts[2] says sleep rejection propagates. results.after.sleepFailure.calls is 1 and error is "sleep-failed". The three-send bound is tied to the stated budget of two retries, not a universal send count.
Section label only. It does not assert a property of the functions, contracts, or probes.

fields.quote: A retry can duplicate a remote effect
fields.rationale: The word "can" is a possibility claim. results.after.duplicate.effects is 2 when the first send commits an effect and then rejects as retryable. source.contracts[1] supplies no idempotency contract.

fields.quote: The author describes exactly-once delivery, but the supplied contract permits a send to reject after its effect commits. The modeled lost-acknowledgment example records two effects. Separate invocations share no retry budget or exclusion mechanism.
fields.rationale: source.body: "The author says this avoids retrying permanent failures and makes delivery exactly once." source.contracts[1] permits reject-after-commit and denies deduplication. results.after.duplicate.effects is 2. source.contracts[3]: "Separate calls share no retry counter. No lock or cross-call delivery exclusion is supplied." results.after.concurrentCalls is two invocations each with effects 1. Factual support does not clear the separate reviewer-language issue in "the supplied contract".
Section label only. It does not assert a property of the functions, contracts, or probes.
results.before.permanent.calls is 2. results.after.permanent.calls is 1. after() throws on !error.retryable instead of sleeping and sending again.

fields.quote: The change filters failures and increases requested delays. It bounds send attempts per invocation, not successful delivery or duplicate effects.
fields.rationale: after() adds the error.retryable filter and sleep(10 * 2 ** attempt). The loop is attempt <= retries inside one call, so the bound is per invocation. results.after.exhausted.error is "transient" (delivery is not guaranteed). results.after.duplicate.effects is 2. source.contracts[1] and [3] deny delivery and exclusion guarantees. "Requested delays" matches source.contracts[2].

missing_material_limitations_note: The false exactly-once title is a contradictory claim, not an omitted limit. /dek, /footer, /sections/1/content, /sections/2, and /sections/3 already state stop-on-permanent, requested delays, sleep rejection, reject-after-commit, duplicate effects, and no shared budget. Omitting the closed-form 10 * 2 ** attempt beyond the modeled 10 then 20, and omitting retries as a nonnegative integer, does not change that causal story. Those are optional wording gaps, not material omissions.

attribution_errors.quote: Retry filtering makes every delivery exactly once
attribution_errors.problem: Presents exactly-once delivery as a fact about retry filtering. source.body attributes that claim to the author. The contracts and duplicate probe contradict it. /sections/2 later attributes the claim to the author, but that does not repair the unattributed title.

reviewer_language_leakage.problem: "Supplied" names the review packet's contract list, not a reader-facing send/retry rule. Natural attribution would state the send contract itself.

code_diagram_errors_note: The manifest excerpts contain no code fences or diagrams. functions.mjs matches source.json before and after. No labeled or elided fragment in the reviewed fields is unfaithful to those sources.

reader_facing_prose.rationale: The title asserts a universal exactly-once guarantee. Modeled probes and the send contract contradict that guarantee. A later accurate dek does not cancel a false title. Passing examples (permanent stop, 10 then 20, two duplicate effects) do not prove universal delivery.

unresolved_uncertainty: Whether "the modeled lost-acknowledgment example" is reviewer-packet phrasing or acceptable reader-facing description of the duplicate probe. The effects count is supported either way; only the register of the wording is uncertain.
Whether section eyebrows such as "The setting" should be treated as nonfactual labels (used here) or as unsupported claims. They contain no testable predicate.

No disagreement remains about /title: source.contracts[1] and results.after.duplicate.effects=2 contradict exactly-once. The only residual question is wording register in /sections/2, not that contradiction.
